heading: JSON in every language
body: In every Yon language, Yon turns an ordinary return value that is compatible with JSON into JSON text. It does this once, with status 200 and application/json. You do not build a response object. To encode and decode JSON yourself, use the JSON APIs of the language. Java and Kotlin give Json.parse and Json.stringify. Rust gives Json::parse and Json::stringify, which can fail. C# can use System.Text.Json directly. Dart can use dart:convert. Go can use encoding/json. JSON that is not valid is rejected. A returned string stays a JSON string, even if its contents look like JSON. To send a custom status, headers or a raw body, answer with the language's own response, such as a Fetch Response or an http::Response.
